strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 QA datasets (NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA) with diverse baselines including RECOMP and NoiseFilter-IB
Pragmatic solution to supervision problem by using downstream task performance as reward signal, avoiding need for expensive compression labels
Strong and consistent empirical results: achieves 3-6% token compression while maintaining or improving EM by 1-7 points across all datasets
Good generalization properties: transfers across compressor architectures (Figure 3), downstream LLMs (Table 2), and generalizes from 5-doc to 10-doc without retraining
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating necessity of both distillation warm-start and GRPO components
Clear presentation with informative visualizations and case studies (Tables 4-5) showing qualitative improvements in summary quality
Practical value: compressor is 9-450x smaller than downstream LLM, reducing computational overhead while maintaining architecture agnosticism
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (GRPO from Shao et al. 2024, standard distillation, QA metrics) without significant innovation in individual components

Misleading 'lossless' framing: claims lossless compression while reducing context from 712→46 tokens (94% reduction) that substantially changes information; more accurate to claim 'effective' or 'beneficial' compression

Insufficient analysis of training efficiency: no wall-clock training time, computational cost, or overhead analysis reported despite requiring downstream LLM inference for every RL rollout during training (5 rollouts × 256 batch size)

Distillation data filtering may introduce bias: uses DeepSeek-V3 supervision and filters examples based on teacher performance, with no analysis of retention rate or distribution shift; could bias toward DeepSeek-V3 summarization style

Reward design lacks justification and exploration: simple weighted sum of EM and F1 with dataset-dependent α hyperparameter (0.2-0.5); no exploration of alternative reward formulations or principled hyperparameter selection

Limited generalization scope: only evaluated on QA with defined answers, small-to-medium LLMs (8-14B), and transfer only to one alternative LLM; unclear if method generalizes to large LLMs or open-ended tasks

Incomplete analysis of learned behavior: beyond two case studies, no systematic investigation of compression patterns, failure modes, or performance across different document types and question complexities
Unfair DeepSeek-V3 comparison: DeepSeek-V3 wasn't task-specifically trained for compression like CORE, making direct performance comparison conflate RL optimization benefits with method superiority

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse QA benchmarks with fair comparisons between methods
Strong generalization properties demonstrated through transferability across different LLMs and robustness to compressor architectures
Well-motivated problem statement clearly articulating limitations of existing compression methods (performance degradation, heuristic-based approaches)
Thorough ablation studies and qualitative case studies (Tables 4-5) providing insights into compression quality
Clear presentation and reproducible methodology with implementation details provided
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily applies existing GRPO algorithm to compression with intuitive task-based rewards rather than introducing methodological advances
Misleading 'lossless compression' framing—paper achieves competitive/slightly improved performance (1-7 EM points), not true losslessness that maintains exact downstream performance
Critical dependence on DeepSeek-V3 (671B) for distillation warm-start undermines 'no predefined labels' narrative and introduces selection bias; no ablation comparing cold-start RL
Modest empirical improvements without statistical significance testing: top-5 compression improvements often 1-3 EM points, with improvements as low as 0.7 points on some datasets
Sparse reward signal inadequately addressed: binary EM reward and token-level F1 (Eq. 4) are crude proxies for semantic correctness; no analysis of how sparsity affects RL convergence
Significant training cost not discussed: 5 rollouts per sample with 14B LLM across multiple epochs on 8 H20 GPUs—cost-benefit analysis absent
Limited analysis of why the method works: no explanation of learned compression patterns, linguistic properties, or mechanisms enabling transferability
Sparse reward design appears ad-hoc: token-level F1 doesn't measure semantic preservation, α hyperparameter choice (0.2-0.5) lacks principled justification
Unfair baseline comparisons: RECOMP and other supervised methods not designed for task-conditioned RL, making direct comparison problematic
Practical limitations underexplored: method requires training separate compressors per task/LLM; scalability and real-world applicability unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical limitations of existing compression methods (3-5 point EM drops)
Sound methodology combining distillation warm-up with GRPO-based end-to-end optimization
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 diverse datasets with both in-domain and out-of-domain compression scenarios
Strong and consistent empirical results: lossless compression (3-6% token ratio) with actual improvements (1-7 EM points) across all datasets
Excellent transferability demonstrated: compression model trained on Qwen2.5-14B generalizes effectively to Llama-3.1-8B without retraining
Robustness across different compressor architectures (1B and 3B models) with consistent performance improvements
Thorough ablation studies convincingly demonstrating necessity of both distillation and GRPO components
Insightful case studies revealing how CORE captures task-critical information better than baselines (Tables 4-5)
Clear, well-organized presentation with effective visualizations of the problem motivation and method pipeline
weaknesses: Distillation warm-up procedure is ad-hoc: filtering logic conflates different training signals (retaining correct-without-summary cases but setting empty targets), and reliance on proprietary DeepSeek-V3 raises reproducibility concerns

Surprising result that compression improves over uncompressed baselines lacks sufficient investigation; claims about 'focusing on key information' need systematic evidence (e.g., analysis of information types preserved, implicit regularization effects)
Limited scope: evaluation restricted to QA tasks; generalization to other downstream tasks (summarization, classification) unclear; unclear if 2-sentence constraint is optimal
Hyperparameter sensitivity requires per-dataset tuning: α is dataset-dependent (Figure 4) with no clear guidance for new tasks; limited sensitivity analysis for other hyperparameters
Insufficient error analysis: only 2 case studies; no systematic investigation of failure modes or dataset characteristics where compression degrades performance
Missing computational cost analysis: no wall-clock training time comparisons, inference latency measurements, or GPU efficiency comparisons relative to baselines
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals reported for results
Conceptual novelty is limited: core contribution is straightforward application of existing GRPO algorithm with task-based rewards; intuitive but not particularly novel

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical RAG efficiency concerns with clear empirical demonstration of the issue
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 datasets with extensive ablations, hyperparameter studies, and robust baseline comparisons
Exceptional generalization results: transfers to longer contexts (5→10 docs), different LLMs (Qwen→Llama), different datasets, and different compressor architectures without retraining
Sound technical approach combining knowledge distillation for warm-start initialization with GRPO-based performance-driven optimization
Practical and efficient design: lightweight compressor module that is easy to deploy with significant computational savings
Clear and well-organized presentation with informative figures and thorough case studies illustrating compression quality
Strong empirical results: achieves 3-6% context compression while matching or improving performance over full-context RAG across all datasets
Good reproducibility: detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, training time, and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward application of existing techniques (distillation + GRPO) rather than novel methodological contributions
Insufficient explanation of core phenomenon: paper doesn't adequately explain why compression can improve performance over full-context RAG, missing opportunity for deeper insights
Narrow scope: evaluation limited to extractive QA tasks with only speculative discussion of open-ended settings and no empirical validation
Distillation dependency: heavy reliance on DeepSeek-V3 as teacher without ablation on teacher quality or exploration of alternative teachers

Unclear training data methodology: paper doesn't clearly specify if RL phase reuses filtered examples from distillation (potential overfitting) or uses fresh examples; filtering statistics not reported
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests despite some improvements being modest (1-2 EM points)
Insufficient hyperparameter analysis: only α studied in detail; sensitivity to other hyperparameters (β, learning rate, G) not explored
Limited failure analysis: case studies show successes but lack investigation of failure modes, systematic errors, or when the method underperforms
Incomplete generalization experiments: length generalization only tested on 5→10 documents; other lengths and generalization patterns not explored
Arbitrary design choices: 2-sentence summary constraint not justified; no sensitivity analysis for prompt template variations
Narrow noise robustness evaluation: only tested on NQ with random document noise; real-world noise patterns and other datasets not comprehensively evaluated
Baseline comparison concerns: DeepSeek-V3 generates 50-92 tokens vs CORE's 32-49, complicating performance comparison; fairness of comparisons with different summary lengths
Incomplete discussion of computational costs: distillation phase using 671B model computationally expensive but cost not thoroughly analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical RAG efficiency concerns with clear motivation and concrete examples
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning 4 QA datasets with extensive ablations, transfer studies, and robustness tests
Strong empirical results achieving 3-6% token compression while maintaining or improving task performance
Practical design treating downstream LLM as black-box, reducing overall computational cost compared to fine-tuning approaches
Demonstrates good generalization to unseen LLMs (Llama vs. Qwen) and cross-dataset transfer with minimal performance loss
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (knowledge distillation + GRPO from prior work) without significant algorithmic innovation or theoretical insights
Task-specific approach with limited generality: evaluation restricted to QA tasks; reward function (EM+F1) is task-specific, and claims about open-ended task applicability are purely speculative

Questionable distillation data filtering using circular criterion (p_summary > p_original); no analysis of retained data fraction or whether teacher→compressor transfer is effective across 671B→1.5B parameter gap

Modest improvements in several cases (HotpotQA: 0.68 EM points; NQ: 2.99 points) raise questions about practical significance, and baseline fairness is unclear (different initialization strategies, unclear tuning efforts)

Incomplete efficiency analysis: no wall-clock time comparisons, superficial training cost analysis, and unaddressed question of whether method generalizes if downstream task/LLM changes (requires retraining)
Incomplete ablation studies: no assessment of distillation necessity (what about random initialization?), teacher model sensitivity, or ablation on reward formulation design
Presentation concerns: critical prompt templates in appendix, only 2 case studies (risk of cherry-picking), and limited statistical rigor (no confidence intervals or significance testing)

strengths: Strong empirical results: 1.5-6.9 EM point improvements across all four datasets while achieving 3-6% token compression, demonstrating consistent effectiveness
Comprehensive evaluation: Thorough assessment across four diverse QA benchmarks with multiple baselines, extensive ablations, generalization tests (different LLMs/datasets), and robustness evaluation
Practical framework design: Lightweight compressor with black-box LLM treatment enables easy deployment; good transferability to unseen LLMs (Table 3) and datasets (Table 4)
Well-motivated approach: Directly optimizing for downstream task performance rather than proxy heuristics is sensible; two-stage pipeline (distillation + GRPO) is well-justified
Thorough experimental documentation: Clear ablations (Table 2), hyperparameter studies (Figure 4), model robustness tests (Figure 5), and qualitative case studies demonstrate scientific rigor
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core components (GRPO, knowledge distillation) are existing methods; contribution is primarily an application to RAG compression rather than methodological advance
Potential data curation bias in distillation: Training data filtered to only examples where teacher summary helps; no analysis of retention rate or impact on learned distribution and generalization

Experimental concerns: (1) DeepSeek-V3 (671B) surprisingly underperforms full-context baseline on some datasets—raises questions about baseline fairness; (2) No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals reported

Restricted evaluation scope: Only evaluated on extractive QA; generalization to open-ended tasks (Section 3.4) is theoretical without empirical validation; improvements are modest in absolute terms (1.5-6.9 points)

Hyperparameter sensitivity and domain dependence: α requires per-dataset tuning (0.2 for HotpotQA, 0.5 for 2Wiki); method optimizes for specific downstream LLM, potentially overfitting to its biases; unclear how to set α in new domains

Incomplete efficiency analysis: Training cost (~5 hours on 8 H20 GPUs) not compared against baseline methods; reliance on expensive DeepSeek-V3 teacher may limit accessibility; scalability to 20+ retrieved documents unexplored
Missing conceptual analysis: Limited investigation of what properties make summaries optimal beyond case studies; no systematic analysis of failure cases or why performance-driven optimization works
